rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites the verse alongside clauses meaning if hardship exists, illustrating the nominative construction with kāna.
rows.anchor: إن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In expressions such as back and belly or plain and mountain, the second noun may be nominative as apposition or emphasis, or accusative in an expanded construction.
rows.anchor: فالبدل أن تقول ضرب عبد الله ظهره وبطنه وضرب زيد الظهر والبطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied sense is on the back and belly or in the plain and mountain; this is not ordinary adverbial syntax and is restricted to established pairs.
rows.anchor: مطروا فى السهل والجبل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Khalīl reports the idiom مطرنا الزرع والضرع; Sībawayh allows its second nouns to be parsed as apposition, emphasis, or accusative.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل ~~رحمه الله أنهم يقولون مطرنا الزرع والضرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nominative forms such as night and day can be understood as apposition or as broad usage in which the time is treated as part of the expression.
rows.anchor: كما قال صيد عليه الليل والنهار وهو نهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jarīr's verse treats night as a named part of the expression, supporting Sībawayh's broad nominative construction.
rows.anchor: فى كل هذا جعل الليل بعض الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the conditional examples, accusative follows one analysis, while nominative is possible when the clause means that truth or falsehood occurs or is present.
rows.anchor: والنصب فيه جيد بالغ على التفسير الأول والرفع على قوله وإن وقع صبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun may be clarified by an explicit body-part noun, as in the phrase about turning a back and belly; the poetry supplies parallel replacements.
rows.anchor: قلت ضرب عبد الله ظهره ومطر قومك سهلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jaʿdī's line permits أهلها to replace the implied people associated with Ḥimyar.
rows.anchor: ما بين حمير أهلها وأوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh distinguishes verbal-noun or direction expressions such as forward and back from place names, which instead involve an omitted preposition.
rows.anchor: فإنما خبر أن الذهاب كان على هذه الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl's line uses place names; the intended sense includes the preposition bi, unlike the verbal-noun examples.
rows.anchor: مكانان وإنما يريد بقنا وعوارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative منطلقين is a circumstantial predicate: it cannot modify only عبدالله or both the two men and عبدالله as an adjective.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا سبيل إلى أن يكون صفة لعبد الله ولا أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative dual منطلقان is also possible when the predicate is understood to describe only the two men, excluding عبدالله.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت قلت هذان رجلان وعبد الله منطلقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With هؤلاء ناس and عبدالله, accusative منطلقين makes a shared circumstantial phrase; nominative منطلقون instead agrees with ناس alone.
rows.anchor: وتقول هؤلاء ناس وعبد الله منطلقين إذا خلطتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sheep-and-lamb example means one dirham for each sheep and its lamb; in this construction the lamb is not included in كل as a definite item.
rows.anchor: وإنما يريد كل شاة وسخلة لها بدرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh prefers راتعين with كل شاة وسخلتها and وهذه ناقة وفصيلها: it is more common and analogical; some Arabs use the alternative nominative.
rows.anchor: والوجه كل شاة وسخلتها بدرهم وهذه ناقة وفصيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mubtadaʾ is the initial noun on which speech is built, and both it and what is predicated of it are nominative.
rows.anchor: فالمبتدأ كل اسم ابتدى ليبنى عليه كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mubtadaʾ requires a predicate that is identical with it or locates it in place or time.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المبتدأ لا بد له من أن يكون

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Khalīl considers predicate-first order such as قائم زيد disfavored unless the fronted adjective is deliberately made the predicate.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أنه يستقبح أن يقول قائم زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Predicate-first adjective phrases are good Arabic when intentionally fronted; if intended as a verb-like assertion, the nominal form is disfavored.
rows.anchor: وأرادوا أن يجعلوه فعلا كقوله يقوم زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A participial noun behaves like a verb only when attached to a described noun or another noun that licenses it; this preserves a distinction between noun and verb.
rows.anchor: وإنما حسن عندهم أن يجرى مجرى الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural body-part nouns can be used for two people because each person's heart is a separate part; the verse uses قلوبكما for two addressees.
rows.anchor: إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural أيديهما is used for the two offenders' hands, distinguishing paired body parts belonging to separate individuals from a single dual object.
rows.anchor: بين المثنى الذي هو شيء على حدة وبين ذا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Khalīl compares plural verb forms for two speakers with the ordinary plural used for three, since the dual is expressed as a kind of plural.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل نظيره قولك فعلنا

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus reports plural forms for two owners, and cites paired persons described with plural verbs; the pattern is also heard from Ruʾbah.
rows.anchor: ضع رحالهما وغلمانهما وإنما هما اثنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account calls the two litigants with plural verbs before naming them as خصمان, showing plural agreement with a dual referent.
rows.anchor: نبأ الخصم إذ تسوروا المحراب إذ دخلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to two addressees is followed by the plural expression إنا معكم, another instance of plural wording for a dual.
rows.anchor: كلا فاذهبا بآياتنا إنا معكم مستمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʾbah's wording ظهراهما and the cited poetry attest plural forms for two distinct but paired things.
rows.anchor: زعم أنه سمع ذلك من رؤبة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Broken plurals such as أقاويل express abundance or emphasis; the simpler plurals أقوال and أبيات suffice when that extra force is not intended.
rows.anchor: لأنك لا تريد بقولك هذه أنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dual forms like عقلان and تمران indicate two distinct kinds; إبلان can mean two herds, while لقاحان سوداوان treats the pair as a dual.
rows.anchor: إلا أن تقول عقلان وبسران وتمران

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Khalīl allows ثلاثة كلاب in poetry by analogy with ثلاثة قرود or as three of the dogs; the poetic examples illustrate numeral constructions.
rows.anchor: وسألت الخليل عن ثلاثة كلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Color adjectives usually follow أفعل, with verbs on فعل يفعل and verbal nouns most often on فعلة; some dialects vary.
rows.anchor: أما الألوان فإنها تبنى على أفعل ويكون الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Color terms also show alternatives such as صدئ يصدأ and غبس/أغبس; غبسة follows the pattern of الحمرة.
rows.anchor: وقالوا صدئ يصدأ صدأة وقالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Colors often form verbs and verbal nouns on إفْعال; frequent forms like احمر and اخضر shorten, while the underlying pattern remains.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنهم يبنون الفعل منه على افعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh relates الصهوبة to أرعن/رعونة and explains البياض and السواد as color terms paired like morning and evening.
rows.anchor: وقالوا البياض والسواد كما قالوا الصباح والمساء لأنهما لونان بمنزلتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some colors use forms such as جون and ورد; their verbal nouns can follow أفعل, while خصيف/أخصف shows another pattern and means blackish green.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء شيء منه على فعيل وذلك خصيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afʿal adjectives also describe diseases and defects, with verbs on فعل يفعل and verbal nouns on فعل; the verse's al-akmah and al-abraṣ fit this class.
rows.anchor: وقد يبنى على أفعل ويكون الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine of an أفعل adjective is فعلاء; Sībawayh lists disease and defect pairs such as أعور/عوراء and آدر.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن مؤنث كل أفعل صفة فعلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أميل is irregular beside مال يميل; the expected verbal noun is ميل, by analogy with الأصيد and صيد يصيد صيدا.
rows.anchor: وقالوا مال يميل وهو مائل وأميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as أشيب/أشمط and أشعر/أجرد express related meanings with different adjective and verb patterns; أزب is also used for hairy.
rows.anchor: وقالوا شاب يشيب كما قالوا شاخ يشيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هوج يهوج and ثول يثول form adjectives and verbal nouns for madness, following the same adjective-building pattern.
rows.anchor: وقالوا هوج يهوج هوجا وهو أهوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mubtadaʾ and its predicate are two necessary parts; neither can replace the other.
rows.anchor: وهما ما لا يغنى واحد منهما عن الآخر ولا يجد المتكلم منه بدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb likewise requires its subject noun, just as the initial noun requires what is predicated of it.
rows.anchor: فلا بد للفعل من الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Particles such as kāna and layta also require a following complement; a noun's initial state is mubtadaʾ until a governing word changes its case.
rows.anchor: ومما يكون بمنزلة الابتداء قولك كان عبد الله منطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vessel's contents may be accusative, genitive directly, or introduced by من; the accusative treats the material as what the vessel contains.
rows.anchor: هذا راقود خلا وعليه نحى سمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material nouns such as طين name a substance rather than an adjective; they may be a circumstantial accusative or a predicate, but وصف خز is bad.
rows.anchor: الطين اسم وليس مما يوصف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A material noun after a governing expression follows noun case behavior; جبتك خزا is a حال, while جبتك خز is predicated of the mubtadaʾ.
rows.anchor: فالحال قولك هذه جبتك خزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In answers like صيد عليه يومان, the days mean that hunting occurred over two days; the preposition is understood through concise, expanded usage.
rows.anchor: يومين ولكنه اتسع واختصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كم in these questions is not itself a temporal adverb: the answer gives the time span, as with offspring born over sixty years or travel over days.
rows.anchor: فليس كم ظرفا كما أن ما ليس بظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question كم ضرب به can be answered with a dual or mass noun for the blows, another concise use of the same question pattern.
rows.anchor: ضرب به ضربتان وضرب به ضرب كثير

words: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to ask the village and caravan means to ask their inhabitants; the action is grammatically applied to the place by ellipsis.
rows.anchor: فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل مكر الليل والنهار means their plotting during night and day, with the time phrase expanded to stand for the omitted relation.
rows.anchor: بل مكركم فى الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means the virtue of the person who believes; البر is understood as بر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر.
rows.anchor: ولكن البر بر من آمن بالله واليوم

words: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِى يَنْعِقُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is to the one being called, not to the caller; the fuller sense is the likeness of caller and called who cannot hear beyond a call.
rows.anchor: فلم يشبهوا بما ينعق وإنما شبهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idioms such as the road treading a people omit أهل, while catching Qanawayn omits a preposition or the game associated with that place.
rows.anchor: بنو فلان يطؤهم الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparisons with أن clauses refer to the person who performs the action, not the action itself, because أن is a noun with its clause as complement.
rows.anchor: أنت أكرم على من صاحب الضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh says al-Jaʿdī uses عذير for a sound or cry; the lines illustrate compressed expressions with a place phrase.
rows.anchor: نعام قاق فى بلد قفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl's line omits bi before place names and connects the verb directly to them.
rows.anchor: وقنا وعوارض يريد بقنا وعوارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāʿidah's line means the fox moved in the road; the preposition في is omitted in the poetic wording.
rows.anchor: فيه كما عسل الطريق الثعلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating a land or town means obtaining and consuming its good things, not literally eating the place.
rows.anchor: أكلت أرض كذا وكذا وأكلت بلدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names such as ظهر, عصر, and مغرب can mean the prayer of that time, while اجتماع القيظ means people gathered during the hot season.
rows.anchor: هذه الظهر أو العصر أو المغرب إنما يريد

rows.speaker: الحطيئة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾah's المنايا phrase means the death of a dead man; the noun is understood as منية ميت.
rows.anchor: وقال الحطيئة # % وشر المنايا ميت بين أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nābighah al-Jaʿdī's comparison means like the relationship or affection of Abū Marḥab, with the relational noun understood.
rows.anchor: وقال النابغة الجعدى # % وكيف تواصل من أصبحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the promise of one of the two groups, أن replaces إحدى الطائفتين and yields the sense that one of the two groups is yours.
rows.anchor: إحدى الطائفتين موضوعة في مكانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second أن clause is an appositional replacement: the generations destroyed do not return to those addressed.
rows.anchor: الذين أهلكناهم إليهم لا يرجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 23:35, أنكم مخرجون replaces the preceding clause about dying and becoming dust and bones; the first أن is fronted to identify the event before resurrection.
rows.anchor: ليعلم ~~بعد أي شيء الإخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same substitution appears in prose with a conditional clause before a second أن; the second clause supplies the promised action.
rows.anchor: أنه إذا أتاك أنه سيفعل وقد علمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن cannot begin independently in this construction as nouns or verbs can; it must remain attached to the preceding statement.
rows.anchor: لأن إن لا تبتدأ في كل موضع

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Khalīl treats the clause about whoever opposes God and His Messenger as the same substitution pattern, while saying فإن would also be good Arabic.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil's verse supports the construction in which a conditional clause is followed by a second أن clause giving the consequence.
rows.anchor: وسمعناهم يقولون في قول ابن مقبل

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports that al-Aʿraj read أنه من عمل منكم سوءا ... فإنه غفور رحيم, a parallel example of the clause construction.
rows.anchor: وبلغنا أن الأعرج قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In forms such as شهد and لعب, the second radical is still unvowelled while the first keeps its original kasra, as if the second radical had moved.
rows.anchor: تسكن العين كما أسكنتها فى علم

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhṭal's line is cited in the pronunciation with شهد and supports retaining the original first-vowel pattern.
rows.anchor: سمعناهم ينشدون هذا البيت للأخطل هكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نعم and بئس are verbs in origin; the related forms فيها ونعمت preserve that pattern, and some Arabs say نعم الرجل.
rows.anchor: نعم وبئس إنما هما فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In غزي الرجل, the yāʾ remains rather than changing to wāw because the form was only lightened from an originally vowelled pattern.
rows.anchor: الأصل عندهم التحرك وأن تجرى ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excepted noun takes accusative because it is removed from the preceding set, is not an adjective, and is governed by the prior clause, like درهما after twenty.
rows.anchor: وانتصب الأب إذ لم يكن داخلا فيما دخل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an affirmative sentence إلا أبوك cannot be an appositional replacement; after negation, ما أتاني القوم إلا أبوك is valid as though the exception alone were stated.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاز ما أتاني القوم إلا أبوك
